newsitem.title: USA: AmEx travel unit Q3 net up nine percent.
newsitem.headline: AmEx travel unit Q3 net up nine percent.

text.p: American Express Co said its travel related services (TRS) recorded net income of $323 million in the third quarter, a nine percent increase over a year ago. The prior year's quarter included income from AMEX Life, a subsidiary sold in October 1995.
Excluding the year-ago results for AMEX Life, net income at TRS grew about 13 percent, revenues increased four percent, and expenses were up two percent.
The company said TRS net revenues reflected an increase in worldwide billed business and growth in cardmember loans outstanding.

American Express said the increase in billed business in TRS resulted in higher spending per cardmember, due in part to its "rewards" incentive programs and increased merchants coverage, as well as an increase in cards outstanding. The increases were partially offset by a decrease in net card fees, reflecting a strategy of growing the lending portfolio through the issuance of low-fee and no-fee credit cards.

American Express said credit quality has improved since last year, particularly in Latin America. American Express said the provision for losses for both charge and lending products declined significantly during the third quarter.
The provision for losses for charge cards declined 16.8 percent to $172 million and the provision for lending products 18.8 percent to $107 million.
American Express said management expects the amount of the fourth quarter provision to be similar to that of the third quarter.

The American Express Financial Advisors unit bad a 17 percent increase in net income to $156 million in the third quarter. An increase in managed assets and growth in distribution fees, primarily from sale of mutual funds, contributed to increases in revenue and earnings.
While sales of mutual funds, life and other insurance products and annuities increased, sales of investment certificates declined from a year ago.
Net income at the American Express Bank unit declined to $18 million in the third quarter from $22 million a year ago. The decline reflected lower revenues partly offset by expense savings.
The company reported total corporate third-quarter net income of $458 million, up 10 percent from a year ago. On a per share basis, earnings rose 14 percent to $0.95 per share.
